svg.title: Fewer bits = a coarser grid, and the outliers pay
svg.desc: A hand-drawn whiteboard: four bit-strips drawn to scale for fp32, bf16, fp16 and int8 with the value 0.1 stored in each and its error written beside it; two number lines showing a weight snapping to the nearest representable value, tiny for fp16 and ten times larger for int4's sixteen levels; a weight-magnitude histogram whose narrow bell is followed by three circled outlier crosses far to the right labelled 0.1% of dimensions up to 20x larger; a crossed-out naive int8 box beside a ticked LLM.int8() box; and a Pareto scatter of GGUF quantizations from q2_K at 3.18 GB scoring 27 out of 50 up to q8_0 at 8.54 GB scoring 43, with the knee highlighted at q4_K_M.
svg.text: Fewer bits = a coarser grid, and the outliers pay
fp16: 1,024 steps between powers of two
int4: 16 levels for the WHOLE block
the same weight - snap error 10x bigger
naive int8: quantize everything the same way
LLM.int8(): outliers stay fp16, the rest go
left of it falls off a cliff:
